name: Shibuya
description: Shibuya, Harajuku and Yoyogi Park, out to Sangenjaya's backstreets: the scramble and Hachiko, the city from SHIBUYA SKY, Center Gai's arcades and the streets a famous game drew.

imagery.attribution: Geospatial Information Authority of Japan (GSI) seamless aerial photographs (GSI terms of use, source attribution)

terrain.attribution: GSI Fundamental Geospatial Data DEM5A, 5 m airborne laser survey bare earth (GSI terms of use); 10 m DEM where 5A is absent

terrain_check.name: GSI elevation API (1 m laser DEM where flown, otherwise DEM5)

plateau.veg_note: PLATEAU's Shibuya-ku survey of single trees has one mesh (53393596), south of the map; the street trees take the heights of Tokyo's surveyed ones (pipeline/plateau_veg.py)
plateau.attribution: MLIT Project PLATEAU Tokyo 23 wards LOD2 building models (CC BY 4.0), as vector tiles by indigo-lab (MIT)

water.note: No sea. The Shibuya River runs in a culvert under the station; its open stretch south of it and the Meguro River from Ikejiri-Ohashi down through Nakameguro are concrete channels drawn at their own level (inland, pipeline/inland_water.py), and so are the parks' ponds.

inland.note: Concrete revetments about 4.5-5 m from the street down to a shallow flow (read from photographs, not measured); the Meguro about 9 m between its walls at Ikejiri-Ohashi and 13 m at Nakameguro, the Shibuya River about 8 m. The ponds at the 5 m laser survey's level.

roofs.note: pipeline/arcades.py (#234): two low PLATEAU-only solids in pedestrian squares (tools/square_huts.py) that the aerial photograph shows are canopies, not huts: a covered walk 3 m wide and 4.1 m tall along the footway by the Yamanote tracks north of the station, and a 2.6 m shelter on an island of the east exit's bus terminal. Each is named by a point inside it, as PLATEAU's footprints have no OSM id.

susuki.note: Susuki (trees.json susuki, #326): on the open grassland and meadows OpenStreetMap maps (natural=grassland, landuse=meadow: the unmown grass of the parks and the hills, where susuki is the grass that stands) (Overture base land, OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL; pipeline/grasses.py). Its heads stand from mid August to spring (web/trees.js).

trees.note: Species are not mapped; the mix is a guess from the cities' street-tree surveys and the parks' own guides: ginkgo and zelkova (keyaki) are Japan's commonest street trees, with plane trees and camphor; the woods are the laurel forest's evergreen broadleaves and camphors, with zelkovas, black pines, maples and a few cedars (sugi, standing for hinoki too). Areas give the parks and precincts known for their own trees a mix of their own; their outlines are OpenStreetMap's (pipeline/tree_areas.py). Somei-yoshino cherries (sakura) line Tokyo's streets after the ginkgo and the zelkova, and stand in the parks' lawns and along the rivers and moats; areas give the places known for them a mix of their own.

areas.name: Hachiko Square's planters
areas.note: The round planter north of Hachiko holds a Somei-yoshino (photographs 2020-25).

areas.name: Hachiko Square's planters, south
areas.note: And so does the one south of him.

areas.name: Meguro River
areas.note: About 800 cherries on both banks from Ikejiri-Ohashi down through Nakameguro, their branches over the water (Meguro City). In the bloom pink chochin hang along both railings and the cherries are lit after dark (#241): the area is the river's line buffered 14 m, so the railings, about 5.5 m either side of it, are 8.5 m inside the outline.

areas.name: Meiji Jingu
areas.note: The planted shrine forest, now mostly camphor and the evergreen oaks and shii of the laurel forest.

tour.title: Sangenjaya to Harajuku
tour.text: Youth culture's Tokyo: fashion on Takeshita Street, the forest of Meiji Jingu, the busiest crossing on Earth, and out west the izakaya alleys of Sangenjaya where the city goes home to drink.

tour.title: The scramble
tour.text: When the lights change, every crossing turns green at once, the diagonals too, and up to three thousand people cross together. Watch it from above, then join in. Hachiko sits to the south, waiting for his master, as he did for ten years.

tour.title: SHIBUYA SKY, 229 m
tour.text: An open-air deck on Scramble Square's roof, glass at the edge and nothing above you but sky. Come at sunset: Mount Fuji on the horizon, then Tokyo lighting up beneath your feet.

tour.title: Sangenjaya's triangle
tour.text: Between Setagaya-dori and Route 246: a bathhouse, a snack bar, a meat shop open all night. A game drew its hero's home town here and called it Yongen-Jaya; fans still come looking for the café.

labels.キャロットタワー: Carrot Tower キャロットタワー

protection.title: No sun-access rule for public places
protection.summary: Tokyo protects no park's sunlight. The windows are a lunch-hour thought experiment for this project, as in the Marunouchi model.
protection.source_note: Windows are our own choice (noon to 13:00, all year), not law. The Building Standards Act's shadow rule (日影規制, art. 56-2) limits hours of shadow on neighbouring land in residential-type zones; it does not cover public places and does not apply in commercial districts such as Shibuya.
protection.reading_note: Tokyo keeps standard time all year. Miyashita Park is a roof garden on a mall (2020): its sun here is read at the ground, so treat it with care.
protection.tip: Tip: try a tower on the block south of Yoyogi Park, west of Harajuku Station.

game.title: Tokyo Pilgrimage: Shibuya 東京巡礼・渋谷
game.blurb: Walk Shibuya under the real sun: the scramble and Hachiko, SHIBUYA SKY 229 m up, Center Gai and Sangenjaya's backstreets, ten years after a game made them famous.

scrambles.note: Koen-dori, the next crossing up; scramble-style (jafmate.jp road trivia, 2023-12-25, which names the scramble-style crossings); diagonals mapped in OSM.

cast.note: the walkers drawn as people, in order (the first six women and six men on a desktop, four and four on a phone): Shibuya's own young crowd in everyday clothes, one office worker in six, and every fourth a visitor from abroad, as on the Scramble (the ward counts it among Tokyo's most visited places by foreign tourists; the share is an estimate)

crowd.note: hours: the share of the peak crowd out, by the hour: the morning commute, lunch, and the evening, busiest from 18:00 to 21:00 and busier still on Friday and Saturday nights and at the weekend (Shibuya Redevelopment Association, 2014: 260,000 people a day on weekdays, 390,000 on holidays); few after the last trains (about 00:30)

look.note: neon: the screens' light on the street (web/neon.js); fill: after dark, the light the crossing's shopfronts, floodlights and signs put on the middle of the scramble, where no street lamp stands (a light card over it, medium and high tiers), the light the square's lamps and shopfronts put on Hachiko from his front (a small warm card aimed at him: the lamps are drawn as points, which do not light a bronze); both are estimates of the light, not luminaires that stand there; sound: the crossing's murmur, its screens' music, the walk signal's bird calls and the station's announcements (web/game/audio.js)

travel.name: Sangenjaya 三軒茶屋
travel.blurb: Sangenjaya's backstreets, the Yongen-Jaya of a famous game: the snack bar New Marina whose front became its café, Chiyo-no-yu and the coin laundry across the lane, Hanamasa's yellow sign, and Carrot Tower over the station.

npcs.name: Aoi 葵
npcs.role: Pilgrimage guide 聖地巡礼ガイド
idle: Ten years since a film and a game drew these streets. This October the pilgrims are everywhere.

npcs.name: Shun 駿
idle: Center Gai never sleeps. It does get quieter around five in the morning.
The arch is real, the burger bar isn't. People still ask.

npcs.name: Yuna 優奈
idle: Lifts from 14F to 45F at 360 metres a minute. Your ears may pop.
The roof closes in strong wind or lightning. Today: {sun_line}

npcs.name: Taro 太郎
idle: Golden hour at SKY EDGE: the towers go copper, then the scramble lights up.

npcs.name: Haru 晴
idle: Sancha, everybody calls it. Three tea houses on the Oyama road, once.
The Setagaya Line's little trams start from the Carrot Tower.

npcs.name: Mr Tanaka 田中さん
npcs.role: A regular at the sentō 常連
idle: Forty years a regular. The water's hotter on the men's side, they say on the women's side.
A bath, then a cold milk from the machine. That's the rule.

lines.title: Report back
lines.on_open: Every walk done. Report back to Aoi by QFRONT, across the scramble from Hachiko.

quests.title: Hachiko
talk: ようこそ渋谷へ! I'm Aoi. I guide pilgrims: people who come to stand where a story stood. This month it's ten years since a film and a game put these streets on the map.

You've just crossed it: the scramble, up to three thousand people at one change of the lights. Hachiko, back across the road, has sat there since 1948, and a game called his square Station Square. Cross back to him when the lights change.
Want to see it from above? The lift at SKY GATE in Scramble Square, just across the road, goes up to SHIBUYA SKY, and a helicopter waits on the roof. A hand up at the kerb (Y) stops a taxi.

steps.text: Meet Shun at the mouth of Center Gai

quests.title: Center Gai
talk: Center Gai. A game called it Central Street and gave it a burger bar that doesn't exist. The arch is real: go and read it.
See the glass passage over the crossing, on the station side? Okamoto Taro's thirty-metre mural, Myth of Tomorrow, hangs inside. A game made that passage a hideout.
For the view everyone came for, go up SHIBUYA SKY on top of Scramble Square. Yuna works the door.

steps.text: Read the arch over Center Gai
Find Yuna at SHIBUYA SKY's street door

quests.title: SHIBUYA SKY
talk: SKY GATE: the lifts run from 14F to 45F at 360 metres a minute. From the 46th floor an escalator takes you out into the open air.
The roof is about 2,500 square metres. The glass is lowest at SKY EDGE, over the scramble. No bags past 46F: the wind takes them.
Press E by the lift door. Or open the map: the roof is on your list of places to go.

steps.text: Ride the escalator out onto the roof
Stand at SKY EDGE, over the scramble

quests.title: SKY EDGE
talk: From up here the scramble is a clock face: everyone waits, then everyone goes.
GEO COMPASS, the raised deck in the middle, points at places you can't see: Mt Fuji, Skytree, Suga Shrine, even Paris and Sydney.
After dark, CROSSING LIGHT: eighteen searchlights. {sun_line}

quests.title: Sangenjaya
talk: Sangenjaya, three tea houses. In a game it's Yongen-Jaya, four: the same backstreets with one more tea house.
The game's café has the front of a snack bar here, New Marina. The bathhouse was Chiyo-no-yu, across the lane: closed now, its board still up.

The pilgrims' walk: up from Route 246 past Pukuichi, the café's lane and the bath's board, the stair corner past the Thai place, the fork where the bars' signs stand and the covered passage, then round to Hanamasa and the batting centre's stair. Each stop stamps your passport.
Take it slow. These are people's homes and small shops.

quests.title: Chiyo-no-yu
talk: Forty years a regular, until it closed in 2021. The board's still up. 千代の湯 入口, Chiyo-no-yu, this way.
The coin laundry was down the alley, vending machines by the door. They boarded it up in the end.
Come back after dark anyway. The signs light up the triangle between Setagaya-dori and Route 246.

quests.title: Pilgrim
talk: お帰り! A crossing, a bathhouse, a roof 229 metres up. All of it real, and now you've stood in all of it.

Ten years ago a game drew these streets. Now you've walked them. The stairs of Your Name are in Shinjuku: two stops north on the Yamanote Line, and my friend Nao guides there. Or change the time, go up SHIBUYA SKY at night, or just wander.

hero.note: The Scramble and Hachiko Square within 100 m of the junction: carriageway, paint, kerbs, pavements, street furniture and the fronts a player sees, modelled finely (cities/shibuya/hero.py, blender/build_hero.py, docs/HERO.md)

story.note: The story (web/game/story.js; docs/STORY.md is the whole of it): Blue Hour. An episode is one case played through in one go: seven frames, each one photograph, on one evening that runs from the blue hour into the night. Sumiko, Akira and what happened on 10 October 1964 are invented; the place, the date, the hours and the city's history are real.
story.title: Blue Hour

card.line: Once an evening, for nine minutes after the sun goes down, the crossing stops. Tonight somebody in it turns to look at you.

afterimage.name: Sumiko 澄子
afterimage.seek: Someone is still moving. Walk to her.
lines: 遅かったね。 You came late.
Sixty years I have stood on this kerb, every tenth of October, at this hour. I was not waiting for you.
He said: the Hachiko crossing, when the sky is the colour of the dome before the show. I was here at fourteen minutes past five. He was not.
Still. You are the first who has ever turned to look. Take this. It is his. There are seven frames left in it.
I cannot see past this kerb any more. Show me what the crossing has become.

goals.shoot: Raise his camera: the screens over the stopped crossing. Turn the wheel to choose the lens.
goals.aim: Turn towards the big screens, then take the picture.
goals.ready: The crossing, stopped, under its screens. Take the picture.

lines: ……So bright. He would have hated it. He counted stars for a living.
He would have come anyway. Something stopped him. Find out what, before the frames run out.

after: The lights change. Nobody else saw the crossing stop.
In your hand, an old rangefinder. Its counter reads 6. Under the base plate a name is scratched: 水野.

meet.goal: A name on a camera. The vintage shop in Center Gai will know what it is.
lines: Where did you get this? Nobody has made one in fifty years.
水野. Mizuno. An owner who scratched his name where only a repairman would find it. A careful man.
And there is a roll in it. Twenty-nine frames gone, seven to go. Whatever he took is still in there, asleep. Film waits.
My grandfather said a roll like this wakes up one frame at a time, if you stand where the man stood. I thought he was drunk. Come back and tell me.

frames.goal: Six frames. Go back out under the arch.

afterimage.name: A shoeshine boy
afterimage.seek: The street has stopped again. Someone by the arch is still moving.
lines: Shine, mister? No. You have his camera.
A man gave me a hundred yen to carry it across to the lady on this corner. A hundred yen, for thirty steps.
He could have carried it himself. He stood right there on the station side and looked at her the whole time.
He had a policeman on each side of him.

goals.shoot: Photograph where the man stood: the kerb on the station side.
goals.aim: Turn towards the station side of the crossing.

lines: He said one thing for me to tell her. I had it ready. Then the policeman looked at me and I ran.
I gave her the camera and I ran. I never said it.

after: He came. He stood across the street between two policemen, and did not cross.
Five frames. On the station side, a police box has stood by Hachiko since before the war.

frames.goal: He was under arrest. Ask at the police box by Hachiko.

afterimage.name: A detective
afterimage.seek: Somebody by the police box is still on duty.
lines: Mizuno Akira, twenty-six. Lecturer at the planetarium. He walked in at four o'clock and said he had pushed a man off its roof.
Kanbara, section chief on the river works. Fell from beside the dome at about ten past three, while the whole city was indoors watching the ceremony.
In twenty years nobody has confessed to me that politely. He asked for one thing: a minute at the kerb, with his camera.
I gave it to him. I have wondered since what he bought with it.
There was a white glove in the dead man's hand. A lift girl's, from the store over the station. Mizuno said it was nothing to do with anyone.

goals.shoot: Hachiko has watched this kerb since before the war. Photograph him, with the station behind.
goals.ready: Hachiko, and the station behind him. Take it.

lines: Behind the dog, over the station: the old store, as it stood that day. A girl in white gloves at the lift doors.
You do not confess that fast to something you did. You confess that fast to keep someone else out of the room.
It was not my case to reopen. It is not mine now.

after: A white glove, a lift girl's. Sumiko ran a lift in that store.
Four frames. The planetarium's roof is gone. The only place it can still be seen from is above.

meet.goal: Go up. The lift at Shibuya Scramble Square, east of the station.
lines: The roof? Forty-five floors in under a minute.
My grandmother ran a lift in the old store over the station. White gloves, a little hat. She said the job never changes: you take people up, and you do not ask them why.
She said one girl went up to the roof on her break, the day of the ceremony, and came down with one glove. Nobody asked her why, either.

frames.goal: Take the lift (E), then the escalator to the roof.

afterimage.name: Kanbara
afterimage.seek: Up here the city has stopped too. One man is still looking down.
lines: You are not him either. I have been waiting for someone to tell me what happened.
I came up for a roll of film. The lecturer photographs the sky from this roof every night, and my works are at the bottom of every picture.
The girl was here instead. I took her wrist; she tore loose, and left me her glove, and ran. I was still on my feet. Write that down.
Then I stood at the parapet watching them draw the rings in the sky, like every fool in Tokyo. Somebody came up the stair behind me.
I never saw who. All I know is whose glove I was holding.

goals.stand: The highest point of the roof: stand at the compass.
goals.shoot: The dome stood where Hikarie stands now, to the east. Look down over the edge and photograph it, with the city lit behind.
goals.aim: Turn east, towards Hikarie, and look down.
goals.ready: The roof where it happened, and all of Tokyo behind. Take it.

lines: What is in it? Tell me.
Two men at the parapet, and five rings half drawn behind them. Ten past three. One of the men is you.
The other has his back to the lens. His shadow falls towards the camera, and the shadow is wearing a site helmet.
A helmet. Not a girl in a pillbox hat. …So it was not her.

after: She shoved a living man and ran. Somebody in a site helmet came up the stair ten minutes later.
Three frames. Kanbara's works: the river that was put under the street, at the foot of this tower. The helicopter on the pad will take you down.

frames.goal: The river runs under the street here, at the foot of the tower.

afterimage.name: Hayase Tatsuo
afterimage.seek: A man in a site helmet is standing where the river went under.
lines: You have been up on the roof. I can see it on you.
A man of mine died in the culvert in September. We were pouring at night to be done before the Games. Kanbara kept it out of the book and paid me to keep it out of my mouth.
On the day, he lost his nerve. He said it would be put on the foreman. On me.
My sister had been up there before me. I did not know that. I found out when they read out what was in his hand.
The lecturer thought she had done it. He walked into the police box before I had got down the stair. I let him.

goals.shoot: He is looking up at what stands on his river now. Photograph it, from the foot to the lights.
goals.aim: Turn to the tower, and look up.
goals.ready: The tower over the river. Take it.

lines: Lamps, a stretcher, a shape under a sheet. So that is what he had on his film. He never knew he had it.
Twelve years he did, for my sister. And she said nothing for sixty, because she thought he had done it for her.
I told her the truth myself, in '89, the week I died. Ask her why she still stands there.

after: Each of them believed the other had done it. Each kept silent to protect the other.
Two frames. By Hachiko, an old man has been watching the camera in your hand all evening.

flight.note: Frame 5's way down: the helicopter off the roof pad, once round over the Scramble, and set down on the open ground north-east of the station, by the river's street. A film whose guide is the helicopter.

caption.text: There is a faster way down than the lift.
From up here the crossing is one thing, breathing in and out.
And under the street east of the station, a river nobody has seen since 1964.

meet.goal: The old man by Hachiko. He knows that camera.
lines: I carried that across this crossing when I was a boy. A hundred yen. You have met me, I think. I was shining shoes.
He gave me one sentence to take to her. Tell her to open it. I saw the policeman looking, and I ran. I have had it in my mouth for sixty years.

He did not die in there. He came out in '76 under his mother's name and took a room in Sangenjaya, fifteen minutes down the line. I shared a bath-house with him for forty years and I never told him either.
Every tenth of October he stood on this kerb at sunset and looked across. He never crossed. He thought he was the worst thing that had happened to her.
He went in March. His will paid for one thing: a photograph of that corner, from this kerb, at fourteen minutes past five today. That was your job tonight. You were a minute late.
The last one he took is still in there. Stand where he stood.

frames.goal: Stand where he stood: the kerb on the station side, facing her corner.

afterimage.name: Mizuno Akira
afterimage.seek: On the station kerb, an old man in the stopped crowd is looking across the road.
lines: Is she there? I can never see past the road.
I thought she had done it. I thought: if I cross to her now, with these two beside me, I make her my reason. So I took her picture, and I sent the boy.
I told him: tell her to open it. She never came. I supposed she had opened it, and decided.
You have my camera. Then take it again. The one I took.

goals.stand: Stand where he stood, at the kerb's edge.
goals.shoot: Face her corner, as he faced it.
goals.aim: Turn to her corner, across the crossing.

lines: Her, at the kerb, twenty-two. Sharp. And in the shop window beside the lens: three men. The one in the middle has his hand up.
Not waving. Holding up two tickets for the last show under the dome. The one we were going to miss the train for.
That was the whole message. I came. I had the tickets. Do not wait. …She never saw it.

after: The answer was inside the camera, in her hands, for sixty years.
One frame. Carry it across to her.

meet.goal: Cross to her kerb. Tell her what was in the camera.
lines: 遅かったね。 You came late.
That was me, the first time, too. You thought it was the girl. She is only what I left here.
Hayase Sumiko. Eighty-two. I have stood at this kerb every tenth of October since I was her.
You have been all over Shibuya with his camera tonight. Before you tell me anything: let me see whether you know.

ask.q: Who was behind Kanbara at the parapet?
ask.wrong: Look at the roof again. The shadow that falls towards the lens is wearing a helmet.
ask.right: Tatsuo. Yes. He told me himself, at the end.

ask.q: Why did Akira not cross the street?
options: He was ashamed of what he had done
He believed I had done it, and would not be seen beside me
The policemen would not let him
ask.wrong: The detective gave him his minute. He could have crossed. Think what the glove told him.
ask.right: And I believed he had done it. For me. So I kept quiet too, so that it would not have been for nothing.

ask.q: What did he send across with the boy?
options: His camera, and a sentence the boy never said
ask.wrong: The boy told you himself, by the arch. And again tonight, by Hachiko.
ask.right: Tell her to open it. He told me once never to open the back of a camera: light kills what is inside. So I never did.

frames.goal: One frame. Find the place where both kerbs are in it.

goals.shoot: Both of them, in one frame. From the middle you can only face one: find the corner that sees both kerbs.
goals.aim: Not yet: one of them is out of the frame.
goals.ready: Both of them. The last frame.

after: Every light at the crossing is green.
In 1964 you could not cross this junction corner to corner. You can now.
An old woman with a clear umbrella is crossing, slowly, through everyone, to the kerb where he stood.

end.title: Blue Hour
end.line: Seven frames, and he is in the last one. The first photograph they were ever in together.
end.next: The counter, at 0, turns over to S. Somebody has loaded a new roll.

overture.note: The episode's cold open, twenty seconds under a clear sky at blue hour (the story keeps its rain for the last frame): the district from the air with every window and screen lit, down to the street from the height of the kerb, the crossing from above as the title falls, then the kerb behind you as the lights change. No guide, no painted filter: the street as it is.

caption.text: Every evening, for a few minutes after the sun goes down, this crossing holds its breath.
Nobody has ever noticed. Tonight, you will.

overture.note: The overture (docs/OVERTURE.md, web/game/overture.js): Crossing. A petal (a ginkgo leaf in autumn, a snowflake in winter, a mote of light in summer) leaves the edge of SHIBUYA SKY, falls 229 m to the scramble, passes Hachiko, and the screens, and ends on the scramble from across it, into the sun, before the game begins at the kerb (game.start). Crowds are kept at a distance: no shot comes close to them. Points name the landmarks in scene.json, so a rebuilt map moves them.

caption.text: The wind on the roof of Scramble Square, above the busiest crossing in the world.
He met his master's train here every evening, and went on waiting for nine years after he was gone.

caption.eyebrow: 渋谷スクランブル交差点 · The scramble
caption.text: When the lights change, up to three thousand people cross at once. Tonight, one of them is you.

night.note: After dark: the night after rain, under a falling star. From the stars down to SHIBUYA SKY and its searchlights, over the edge of the roof and down to the scramble, to Hachiko under the lamps, the screens in the wet street, the hush before the lights change, and the crossing itself. The crowd is seen from above and from across the junction; no shot stands among it. wet: the streets wet from a shower that has passed, under a clear sky. show: CROSSING LIGHT on whatever the hour. One meteor crosses the sky, and only where the sky is empty (from the roof, and over the title), never with the searchlights' beams in shot: a comet standing among the searchlights' beams read as a moon throwing light (the owner, November 2026).
